mainTopic: Torn hides, meat entering and leaving a house of עבודה זרה, and business with people going to an idolatrous festival
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of hides torn opposite the heart, a sign that the animal may have been killed for עבודה זרה. A teaching says a hide with no trace of blood is permitted, and רב הונא limits this to a hide that was never salted, since salt could have drawn out the blood. שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who forbids only a round tear. אביי asks whether that ruling means the חכמים really disagree, and he insists that understanding matters even when the practical law stays the same. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's rule on meat. Meat going into a house of עבודה זרה is permitted, which cannot follow רבי אלעזר. Meat coming out is forbidden, because some of it was surely offered, and this follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who compares idolatrous offerings to a מת. Finally, שמואל explains the ban on doing business with people going to a תרפות: for a גוי it applies on the way there, and for a ישראל on the way back, with the reason continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: A torn hide with no trace of blood is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier teaching about hides torn opposite the heart: if there is no trace of blood on the hide, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is no trace of blood on the hide, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the teaching that defines hides torn opposite the heart. It is setting up רב הונא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same teaching said that a torn hide with a trace of blood is forbidden. Here is the other side: with no blood, the hide is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: a trace or small drop of blood

phrases.english: If there is no trace of blood on it — it is permitted.
phrases.notes: "It" is a hide torn opposite the heart, the case being discussed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's definition of hides torn opposite the heart, which רב הונא will comment on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A torn hide with no trace of blood is permitted.

steps.title: רב הונא: the leniency applies only if the hide was not salted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the teaching just quoted. A bloodless hide is permitted only if it was not salted, because salt could have removed the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: This was taught only when the gentile did not salt the hide. If he salted it, it is forbidden, because I can say the salting took the blood away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא narrows the leniency just quoted. It only counts when the hide was never salted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having no blood shows the animal was not killed for עבודה זרה only if nothing else could have removed the blood. Salt draws out blood, so on a salted hide the missing blood proves nothing, and the hide stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: they only taught this in the case of... (a limiting formula)
I can say; one might suggest

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
They taught this only where he did not salt it,
but if he salted it — it is forbidden.
For I can say: its salting removed it.
phrases.notes: "It" here is the trace of blood, which the salt may have drawn out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא מְלָחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the leniency of the teaching quoted in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bloodless torn hide is permitted only if unsalted. A salted one is forbidden, since the salt may have removed the blood.

steps.title: The משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on round versus long tears
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה: a round tear makes the hide forbidden, and a long tear leaves it permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: When the tear is round, the hide is forbidden. When it is long, the hide is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It is setting up a ruling about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a sign based on the shape of the tear. Only a round tear around the heart points to עבודה זרה. A long tear does not, so that hide is permitted.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
When its tear is round — it is forbidden,
if long — it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a round tear makes the hide forbidden. A long tear leaves it permitted.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling: we follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the shape of the tear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, then, only a round tear forbids the hide. This ruling becomes the starting point for אביי's question in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law: a long tear does not make a hide forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the opinion quoted in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: אביי asks whether the ruling implies a disagreement
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether saying 'the הלכה follows' him means the חכמים actually disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: When you say 'the הלכה follows him,' does that imply that others disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a clarifying question about how to read שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling that the הלכה follows someone usually suggests someone else argues. אביי wants to know whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is really disputing the חכמים, or only explaining what everyone already holds.

keyTerms.meaning: by implication, from which we infer

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
"Halakha" — does that imply that they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים, the first opinion in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הֲלָכָה — מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'הלכה כ...' mean there is a real disagreement between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the חכמים?

steps.title: רב יוסף: what difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף pushes back: either way the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so why does it matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: What difference does it make to you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brushes off the question as having no practical effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether or not the חכמים disagree, the practical law stays the same. So רב יוסף sees no reason to settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: what practical difference does it make to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי נָפְקָא לָךְ מִינַּהּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: What difference does it make to you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי נָפְקָא לָךְ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dismisses אביי's question in step 5 as having no practical effect
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the need to answer אביי's question at all
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question changes nothing in practice.

steps.title: אביי: learning is not just singing a tune
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a saying: should we just repeat what we learned like a song, without understanding it?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Learn the lesson, and let it be a song?' We must understand the learning, not just repeat it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his question. Understanding the learning matters even when the practical law stays the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי rejects the idea that only practical results count. Knowing whether a real disagreement exists is part of truly understanding the משנה, not just memorizing a ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי teaches that we study to understand, not only to know the practical bottom line. A question with no practical difference is still worth asking.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גְּמָרָא גְּמוֹר, זְמוֹרְתָּא תְּהֵא?
phrases.english: He said to him: "Learn the lesson" — should it be like a song?
phrases.notes: This is a popular saying: should learning just be memorized like a tune, without understanding?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גְּמָרָא גְּמוֹר, זְמוֹרְתָּא תְּהֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's pushback in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Understanding matters even without a practical difference, so the question is worth asking.

steps.title: The משנה: meat entering a house of עבודה זרה is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: meat brought into a house of עבודה זרה is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat that goes into a house of עבודה זרה is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about who taught it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that simply bringing meat into the house of עבודה זרה does not make it forbidden. The next steps ask which תנא holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: idol worship; here, its house of worship

phrases.english: Meat that enters idol worship is permitted.
phrases.notes: "Enters idol worship" means brought into the house where the idol is worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat brought into a house of עבודה זרה is permitted.

steps.title: Who taught this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that meat entering a house of עבודה זרה is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking 'מאן תנא' signals that this ruling does not fit every תנא. The גמרא wants to find which opinion it matches or clashes with.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא (teacher of the משנה) that taught this?

phrases.english: Who taught it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the משנה quoted in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that meat entering a house of עבודה זרה is permitted?

steps.title: Not like רבי אלעזר, who says a gentile's plain intent is for עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר holds that a gentile's unstated intention is for עבודה זרה, so he would forbid the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is not like רבי אלעזר. If it were like רבי אלעזר, there is a problem, because he says a gentile's plain intention is for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה cannot follow רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that when a gentile slaughters without saying why, we assume he meant it for עבודה זרה. By his view the meat would already be forbidden, so he could not say it is permitted. The משנה must follow a different view.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the meat is forbidden in practice. He is only saying the משנה's ruling cannot match רבי אלעזר's view.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Elazar,
for if it were in accordance with Rabbi Elazar — doesn't he say:
A gentile's unspecified intention is for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's question by ruling out רבי אלעזר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה does not follow רבי אלעזר, who assumes a gentile's plain intention is for עבודה זרה and so would forbid the meat.

steps.title: Meat coming out of a house of idol worship is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: meat that comes out of a house of עבודה זרה is forbidden, because it is like 'offerings to the dead.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And meat that comes out is forbidden, because it is like offerings to the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second half of the משנה's line. Meat going in was permitted, but meat coming out is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a short reason: the meat is 'like offerings to the dead' (זבחי מתים). The next steps will explain why we assume this meat was offered, and whose opinion uses this phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: That which comes out (here, meat leaving the house of עבודה זרה)
Offerings to the dead, a name for idolatrous offerings

phrases.english: And [meat] that comes out is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is the other half of the line from Step 8. Meat going in is permitted; meat coming out is forbidden.

phrases.english: because it is like offerings to the dead.
phrases.notes: 'The dead' here means idols. The פסוק quoted soon uses this exact phrase.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיּוֹצֵא אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְּזִבְחֵי מֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the discussion of meat going in, and quotes the ruling on meat coming out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat leaving a house of עבודה זרה is forbidden, as it is like זבחי מתים.

steps.title: Why is the outgoing meat treated as an offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that meat coming out is treated as 'offerings to the dead.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why meat coming out is automatically treated as an idolatrous offering. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat going in might never have been offered. So why should meat coming out be any different? The גמרא wants the logic behind the משנה's ruling.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why outgoing meat is assumed to be an idolatrous offering.

steps.title: It surely contains an idolatrous offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is impossible that this meat does not include some idolatrous offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is impossible that there is no idolatrous offering in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that once meat has been inside the house of עבודה זרה and comes out, we assume some of it was offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before it goes in, the meat has not been used yet. After it comes out, we can be sure some of it was offered to the idol. That is why only the outgoing meat is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to an idol

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלֵיכָּא תִּקְרוֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: It is impossible that there is no idolatrous offering [in it].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלֵיכָּא תִּקְרוֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Meat coming out certainly includes some idolatrous offering.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that idolatrous offerings are 'like offerings to the dead.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא this part of the משנה follows. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling idolatrous offerings 'like the dead' is a specific comparison. The גמרא wants to know which תנא makes that comparison.

phrases.english: Whose [opinion] is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the reason, the גמרא asks who the source is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא compares idolatrous offerings to the dead.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the opinion of רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא: רבי יהודה בן בתירא. The next step brings the ברייתא that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא only gives the name. The proof that רבי יהודה בן בתירא compares offerings to the dead comes right after.

phrases.english: It is [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

steps.title: The ברייתא: idolatrous offerings are compared to a dead body
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה בן בתירא learns from a פסוק that an idolatrous offering makes things טמא through אהל, just like a dead body.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: From where do we know that an idolatrous offering makes things טמא through a tent? As it says: 'They joined themselves to בעל פעור and ate offerings of the dead.' Just as a dead body makes things טמא through a tent, so too an idolatrous offering makes things טמא through a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה בן בתירא compares idolatrous offerings to a dead body. That comparison matches the משנה's words 'like offerings to the dead.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls idol offerings זבחי מתים, 'offerings of the dead.' From this רבי יהודה בן בתירא compares them fully to a מת, even for the special טומאה of אהל. Because his comparison is complete, the offering is also forbidden to benefit from, just like a מת, which is the משנה's point about the outgoing meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes things טמא by being under the same roof, even without touching
A well-known idol from the time of the desert

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the משנה's phrase 'like offerings to the dead' is not just a figure of speech. It is a real comparison taught by a specific תנא.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
From where [do we know] that an idolatrous offering
makes things impure through a tent?
phrases.notes: Anything under the same roof becomes טמא, even without touching it.

phrases.english: As it is stated:
"They joined themselves to Baal Peor
and ate offerings of the dead,"
Just as a dead body makes things impure through a tent,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תִּקְרוֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מְטַמְּאָה בְּאֹהֶל.
phrases.english: so too an idolatrous offering makes things impure through a tent.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim of Step 15 by quoting רבי יהודה בן בתירא's ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's phrase 'like offerings to the dead' follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה בן בתירא compares idolatrous offerings to a מת, based on תהלים 106:28.

steps.title: No business with people going to an idolatrous festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: it is forbidden to do business with people going to a תרפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those going to an idolatrous festival: it is forbidden to do business with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה, about doing business with people traveling to an idolatrous festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic. The משנה forbids business with people going to a תרפות. The next step, from שמואל, will explain exactly when this applies.

keyTerms.meaning: To do business (literally, to take and to give)

phrases.english: Those going to an idolatrous festival —
it is forbidden to do business with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוֹלְכִין לַתַּרְפּוּת אֲסוּרִין לָשֵׂאת וְלָתֵת עִמָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after finishing the discussion of the meat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Business with people going to a תרפות is forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל: a גוי on the way there versus on the way back
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that with a גוי going to a תרפות, business is forbidden on the way there and permitted on the way back.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A גוי going to an idolatrous festival: on the way there it is forbidden, because he goes and gives thanks before the idol. On the way back it is permitted, because what happened already happened.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains the משנה for a גוי. The ban applies only while he is on his way to the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the way there, a good business deal could lead him to thank his idol at the festival. On the way back the worship is already over, so refusing to deal with him changes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What was, was (it is already done)

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A gentile who goes to an idolatrous festival,
on the way there, it is forbidden,
because he goes and gives thanks before the idol,
on the way back, it is permitted,
what was, was.
phrases.notes: He means the worship is already over, so holding back now would not stop anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's ban for a גוי to the trip there only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a גוי going to a תרפות, business is forbidden on the way there and permitted on the way back.

steps.title: שמואל: a ישראל going to an idolatrous festival is the opposite
steps.stepSummary: שמואל continues: for a ישראל, business is allowed on the way there, since he might change his mind, but forbidden on the way back.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ישראל going to an idolatrous festival: on the way there it is permitted, because perhaps he will change his mind and not go. On the way back it is forbidden, since...
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the rule for a Jew going to a תרפות, and it is the reverse of the rule for a גוי. The reason for the ban on the way back continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jew on his way may still change his mind, so we do not yet treat him as an idol worshipper. On the way back business is forbidden, but the text breaks off at 'since' (כֵּיוָן), and the reason comes on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. For a גוי, business is forbidden on the way there and allowed on the way back. For a ישראל, it is the exact opposite.

phrases.english: A Jew who goes to an idolatrous festival —
on the way there, it is permitted,
perhaps he will change his mind and not go;
on the way back, it is forbidden, since

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שמואל's statement with the opposite rule for a Jew.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a ישראל going to a תרפות, business is permitted on the way there and forbidden on the way back.
